product.schneider-towerat201.summary: The entry-level Tower AT with one floppy drive and no standard hard disk.
product.schneider-towerat201.history: Tower AT 201 was the entry configuration in Schneider's compact range, documented in 1988. It shared its design with the 202 and 220 but relied on a single floppy drive. The package targeted DOS work with included software, in a case that could also lie horizontally. The manual identifies Schneider electronics but does not establish an external OEM contractor.
product.schneider-towerat201.technical.c: The base configuration distinguishes it from the 220. The 201 is identified with one 720 KB floppy drive. Happy Computer tested a diskless Tower for about 2,500 DM in 1988 without naming its suffix: this is not a confirmed 201 launch price.
product.schneider-towerat201.technical.f: Family ROMs are not a confirmed 201 dump. The historical record named towerat201 holds towerat2xx sets; some provenance identifies a 220 or 240 Mega. Physical attribution to a 201 remains missing.
product.schneider-towerat201.warning: Historical sheet under research; booting in BluMach remains unvalidated.
product.schneider-towerat201.technical.v: Sources and file hashes have been checked. BluMach a1b0125d has no dedicated entry for this model; MAME groups Tower AT 2xx machines as not working. Booting has not been tested.
product.schneider-towerat201.technical.l: The complete machine still needs validation. Board, BIOS pair and video ROM must be identified, then POST, memory, keyboard, RTC, disks and ports tested before usable emulation can be claimed.
product.schneider-towerat201.technical.b: The CPU and memory occupy a separate card. The 201/202/220 manual documents Tower CPU286 50229, GC101/GC102 logic, DS1287 RTC and 8042/8742 keyboard controller; it includes different circuit revisions.
product.schneider-towerat201.technical.m: Expansion depends on the installed board. The manual diagram shows a 512 KB base and optional DIL/SIMM banks; it does not prove that every unit has the connectors fitted.
product.schneider-towerat201.technical.v: Integrated video leaves expansion slots available. The 1988 review documents EGA and up to 800 × 600 with a multisync monitor and suitable software; it counts three 16-bit slots and one 8-bit slot.
product.schneider-towerat201.technical.m: Schneider, Service Manual Tower AT 201/202/220, Ident-Nr. 44657, 03/1989: cover and CPU/memory diagrams reviewed; PDF preserved.
product.schneider-towerat201.technical.r: Happy Computer 11/1988, M. Ohnesorg/rz, Rechengiganten zu Niedrigpreisen, pp. 97–98 and 101: review of a Tower AT without a hard disk, with no commercial suffix identified.
product.schneider-towerat201.technical.m: Happy Computer 05/1989, Sammlerstück, p. 18: 220 Mega edition, equipment, prices and announced production run; scan and transcription preserved.
product.schneider-towerat201.technical.r: Jungsi, Schneider VGA AT System 40: range overview and approximate chronology; not a substitute for a manual covering each revision.
product.schneider-towerat201.technical.m: MAME, at.cpp: towerat2xx sets, variant provenance and unresolved EGA pairings. Files are preserved in the library; their presence does not prove universal compatibility.
product.schneider-towerat201.technical.c: BluMach a1b0125d, inspected and preserved machine table: no dedicated Tower AT entry.
